value.name: distinguish codicil from letter
value.description: Rosa explains that the codicil and the letter are different documents, with the codicil carrying legal force and the letter expressing a wish.
evidence: They do not say the same thing. The codicil is the law. The letter is the wish.

I have been a housekeeper for thirty-one years and I have a great deal of respect for the difference between the law and the wish. The law is what protects you. The wish is what asks something of you. They are not enemies. But they are not the same.

value.name: Rosa rejects wanting the house
value.description: Rosa states plainly that she does not want the house, prompting Lucia and Daniel to react silently.
evidence: "I do not want the house," she said.
Lucia drew in a breath. Daniel did not move.

value.name: Rosa clarifies she cannot take the house
value.description: Rosa explains that she does not want the house in the sense of taking it from Lucia and Daniel or entering an emotionally destructive transaction.
evidence: "I want you to listen to me," Rosa said, "before you decide what I mean. I do not want the house in the sense that I cannot afford the house and I do not wish to spend my old age in a transaction with the two of you that I would not survive emotionally. I do not want the house in the sense of taking it from you. I am not capable of that and I would not become capable of it."

value.name: Rosa asks to remain in the house
value.description: Rosa says she does not want to leave and asks to keep living in her third-floor room while continuing to cook in the kitchen.
evidence: "But I do not want to leave the house either. I have lived in the third-floor room since 1996. I would like to continue to live in the third-floor room. I would like to continue to cook in this kitchen, not for wages, because I will not be a housekeeper here any longer, but because I do not know how to be in a kitchen and not cook in it."

value.name: Rosa requests a named room and key
value.description: Rosa asks that one of them keep the house and that a room be reserved for her in the legal document with her own key.
evidence: "I would like, if it is possible — and I am asking, I am not telling — I would like for one of you to keep the house. I do not care which one. I would like, in whatever arrangement you make between you, for there to be a room in it for me, named in the document, with a key that is mine and not loaned to me"
